result.rule: When the description states that one party performs two activities joined by 'and', with no stated order between them, and both must be finished before the next described step: Model the two activities as parallel branches: place a parallel gateway split before them, connect each activity to a parallel gateway join, and continue from the join to the next step. Do not sequence the activities one after the other unless the description orders them, and do not put an exclusive gateway between them.

When the description says that, while several parallel activities run for the same case, one actor also performs a separate action that is not part of those activities, and the later step must wait for this action as well.: Model that separate action as its own task on a dedicated parallel branch that starts at the same parallel gateway as the other parallel activities. Rejoin all branches at one parallel gateway before the later step that depends on them. Do not fold the action into another task or into the task that precedes the split, and do not omit it.

When the description says several activities are performed independently of each other and all of them must be completed before a later step can begin: Model a parallel gateway that splits the flow into one branch per independent activity, and a parallel gateway that joins those branches so the later step starts only after all of them finish. Do not leave the branches unsynchronized, and do not use an exclusive gateway for a join that requires every branch.

When the description says that several activities or item branches start at the same time after one point, and that a following step begins once the first of the concurrently arriving items is available, while the remaining items keep arriving in an unspecified order and must not hold up that step: Open the concurrent activities and item branches with a parallel gateway split placed before them, with one outgoing flow per branch and no conditions on those flows. Model the junction before the first-arrival step as a complex gateway that continues on the first incoming token, not as a parallel join that waits for every branch. Keep the handling of the remaining arrivals on their own branches, linked to the process so they do not block the continuation.
